info.title: Database API
info.description:
# API Overview The API utilizes a [RESTful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer) architecture, allowing you to query and manage data from the AppFolio ecosystem. All API requests and responses are formatted in `application/json`, and HTTP Basic Auth or OAuth Client Credentials is used to verify a user's identity. The base URL for all API requests is `https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/{endpoint}`. To kick start your API usage, we recommend diving into our *Getting Started* section(s), depending on your selected authentication flow. Depending on your selected authentication flow, this section takes you through a standard API use case. Review the *API Best Practices* section to optimize your API usage and ensure seamless integration into your application. # Authentication We support two authentication methods for accessing the API: 1. OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials 2. HTTP Basic Authentication (Legacy) # OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials - BETA **BETA - This feature may have limitations or unexpected behavior as we continue to improve it based on customer feedback.** OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials is a token-based authentication system that obtains credentials, validates them to generate an access token, and then uses that token for subsequent API requests. Our OAuth implementation introduced additional per-attribute and per-database scopes. With OAuth you'll benefit from: - Ability to generate multiple credentials - Scoped granular access per credential, restricting the endpoints and attributes accessible by a credential - Enhanced security through temporary access tokens that expire after 5 minutes - Ability to assign a credential to a specific user ### Required Headers | Name | Format | Value | |-------------------------|--------|-------------------------| | Authorization | string | Bearer `{access_token}` | | X-AppFolio-Developer-ID | string | `{YOUR-DEVELOPER-ID}` | | X-AppFolio-Database-ID | string | `{YOUR-DATABASE-ID}` | ## Getting Started: OAuth Client Credentials 1. **Get Your OAuth Credentials** - Beneath API Credentials Select OAuth - Select New API Credential to generate your OAuth Credential - Enter an OAuth Credential Name & Purpose - Select the Databases the credential can access - Assign the credential to either All Administrators and Production Users or a specific user - Specify which endpoints and attributes this credential will have access to - Upon creation, securely store your new OAuth generated credentials consisting of a Client ID and Client Secret 2. **Get Your Developer ID and Database Id** - Navigate to your newly created credential - Save the value of the Developer ID at the top of the page for later reference - Save the Database ID to be used in your API Requests 3. **Request an Access Token via cURL** ``` curl -X POST 'https://api.appfolio.com/oauth/token' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \ --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \ --data-urlencode 'client_id={YOUR-CLIENT-ID}' \ --data-urlencode 'client_secret={YOUR-CLIENT-SECRET}' ``` Replace in the above command: - `{YOUR-CLIENT-ID}` with your Client ID - `{YOUR-CLIENT-SECRET}` with your Client Secret 4. Use the Access Token in your API Requests, which includes the three required headers. ``` curl -g --request GET 'https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0{resource}' \ --header 'X-AppFolio-Developer-ID: {YOUR-DEVELOPER-ID}' \ --header 'X-AppFolio-Database-ID: {YOUR-DATABASE-ID}' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer {YOUR-ACCESS-TOKEN}' ``` Replace in the above command: - `{YOUR-DEVELOPER-ID}` with your Developer ID - `{YOUR-DATABASE-ID}` with your Database ID - `{YOUR-ACCESS-TOKEN}` with the access token obtained from Step 3 **Note**: Access tokens expire after 5 minutes. Request a new token when it expires. When writing your integration code to refresh the API token, use the value in the access token request: `expires_in` in seconds. This value is currently 5 minutes but is subject to change. # HTTP Basic Authentication (Legacy) HTTP Basic Authentication is a simple authentication scheme where credentials (Client ID and Client Secret) are encoded in Base64 format and included in each API request's header, requiring separate credential pairs for each customer database you need to access. While still supported, Basic Authentication requires: - Separate credentials for each customer database - Manual onboarding process for each new customer - Storing permanent credentials securely - Managing multiple sets of credentials across different customer databases ### Required Headers | Name | Format | Value | |-------------------------|---------|--------------------------| | Authorization | string | Basic `{ENCODED-STRING}` | | X-AppFolio-Developer-ID | string | `{YOUR-DEVELOPER-ID}` | ### **Migration Note** Legacy Basic Auth credentials will remain active, allowing you to transition to OAuth at your own pace. We strongly recommend adopting OAuth for new integrations and planning to migrate existing integrations to take advantage of its improved security and simplified credential management. If you need to maintain an existing integration, see the OAuth Client Credentials Guide or the HTTP Basic Auth Guide for details on implementation. ## Getting Started: HTTP Basic Authentication (Legacy) 1. Get Your Developer ID - Select your account name → Admin → Developer ID in the Developer Details card 2. Get Your Basic Auth Credentials - Beneath **API Credentials**, select **Basic Auth** - Generate and securely store your **Client Secret** on the same row by selecting **Generate a Client Secret**. Store this value in a safe place. 3. Generate the Base64 Encoded Credentials - For **Mac** users, paste the following command with your Client ID and Client Secret in **Terminal**: ``` echo -n "{ClientID}:{ClientSecret}" | base64 ``` - For **Windows** users, paste the following command with your Client ID and Client Secret in **Windows Command Prompt**: ``` powershell "[convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("{ClientID}:{ClientSecret}"))" ``` Replace in the above commands: - `{ClientID}` with your Client ID - `{ClientSecret}` with your Client Secret 4. Make an API Request ``` curl -g --request GET 'https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/{resource}/' \ --header 'X-AppFolio-Developer-ID: {YOUR-DEVELOPER-ID}' \ --header 'Authorization: Basic {YOUR-ENCODED-STRING}' ``` Replace in the above command: - `{YOUR-DEVELOPER-ID}` with your Developer ID - `{YOUR-ENCODED-STRING}` with the value returned from step 3 - `{resource}` with the desired resource (for example, properties, tenants, or charges) **Note**: You'll need separate credentials for each customer database when using Basic Auth. # Rate Limits To prevent network congestion and avoid `429` **Too Many Requests** errors, we recommend regulating or staggering the rate of your requests. All endpoints have per-second, per-minute and per-hour global rate limits for each set of credentials.
Currently, the rate limits are as follows: - **8 requests per second, 256 requests per minute, and 4096 requests per hour** Some endpoints have a separate, stricter rate limit: - The **General Ledger Details** endpoint (`/gl_details`) is limited to **5 requests per 15 seconds**. - The **Jobs** endpoint (`/jobs`) is limited to **5 requests per 15 seconds**. # Error Codes The API returns HTTP status codes. The following error codes are possible. | Error Code | Text | Description | |------------|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `400` | Bad Request | The request was not processed due to invalid syntax. | | `401` | Unauthorized | HTTP Basic: Access denied. | | `403` | Forbidden | The developer has insufficient permissions to access this API endpoint. | | `404` | Not Found | The requested resource could not be found. | | `409` | Conflict | The request conflicts with the current state of the resource. Resolve the conflict and retry. | | `422` | Unprocessable Entity | The request was understood, but not processed due to semantic errors. Ensure that the parameters contain valid values. | | `429` | Too Many Requests | The developer has sent too many requests. | | `500` | Unexpected Error | The server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented a successful request. This is usually a temporary state. | | `503` | Service Unavailable | The server cannot handle the request due to overload or maintenance. Please try again later. | | `533` | Data Unavailable | Data is currently unavailable. Please try again later. | | `701` | Invalid Credential | The customer has restricted access to their data by disabling their API integration. | # API Best Practices To maximize efficiency and ensure the reliability of your integration with the API, review the following best practices. ## Date and Time Formatting Our API strictly adheres to the ISO 8601 format for `` representation, which follows the pattern `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ` for date and time, where "T" separates the date and time components, and "Z" indicates Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). This global standard ensures clarity and consistency across different systems and programming languages. By following ISO 8601, developers can avoid ambiguity and facilitate seamless integration with our API. `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` - `YYYY` is the four-digit year - `MM` is the two-digit month - `DD` is the two-digit day - `T` separates the date and time components - `hh` is the two-digit hour - `mm` is the two-digit minute - `ss` is the two-digit second - `Z` indicates Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) - `2022-06-00T12:00:00Z` is equivalent to June 1st, 2022, at 12:00:00 PM UTC. ## Deprecation When reading the API documentation you will notice attributes marked as **Deprecated**. When an attribute or endpoint is marked as **Deprecated**, we no longer recommend using it due to changes in the API. Any new API users should not use deprecated attributes, and existing API users should consider transitioning to updated attributes or endpoints. When a new API version is released in the future, the deprecated attributes or endpoints will be removed entirely. ## Filtering and Pagination To ensure the proper utilization of the `LastUpdatedAt` query parameter, we recommend the following best practices: - The `LastUpdatedAt` attribute indicates the date of the most recent update to an object in the AppFolio Property Manager. However, changes may not always be visible to API users, as they could involve internal attributes or attributes that are inaccessible to certain users. API users should not make assumptions about what changed on an object based solely on the fact that `LastUpdatedAt` has changed. Rather, they should compare the changed object's attributes to the last known attributes to discover the change if needed. - For the first import using a given endpoint, you may want to set the `LastUpdatedAt` filter to a date in the past (e.g. `filters[LastUpdatedAtFrom]=1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`) and use the response to sync up your internal records. If this response has more than one page, you will need to fetch the following pages as well. For subsequent requests following the initial import, avoid setting arbitrary parameters for `LastUpdatedAt` and instead set this value to the last time you made a successful request. This will improve performance by only retrieving the data you need, and subsequently reducing the time it takes to receive the response. To ensure the proper utilization of the `page` query parameter, we recommend the following best practices: - If possible, use the default value for the `page` query parameter. The default values were carefully selected to ensure that unnecessarily large requests are not sent. The default value for the `page` size parameter is 1000, but this might differ per endpoint. The page size parameter can be modified to a smaller number if desired. If page sizes larger than the default page size parameter are requested, page size will be reduced to the default value. AppFolio can reduce or increase the default page size parameter for a given endpoint. The following is an example of a valid request with the default values for the `page` query parameter: - `https://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/{resource}?filters[LastUpdatedAtFrom]=1970-01-01T00:00:00Z&page[number]=1&page[size]=1000` ## Outages As with any API, errors and exceptions will occur. For example, there may be a connection error between servers or a rare outage. Always watch for errors and exceptions, and if they do occur, log the request in as much detail as possible. This will reduce response times in the event that you need to contact support. - In the event of a `503` **Service Unavailable** error, we suggest implementing [Exponential Back Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_backoff). This ensures that your server does not generate excessive load. - A `533` **Data Unavailable** error typically occurs when a database is down due to database migrations and/or scheduled maintenance. Scheduled maintenance errors will typically resolve within five minutes, and will occur between 9PM and 4AM PST. ## Retry-After Header: Retrying Rate Limited API Requests A `Retry-After` HTTP response header is utilized by AppFolio to manage rate-limited API requests. When your request is rate limited, this header indicates the time duration in seconds that you should wait before resending the request. It is best practice to observe the value of the `Retry-After` header and wait for the specified time to resend the request. Adhering to this guidance will reduce the number of 429 "Too Many Requests" errors sent, and conserves resources for both your integration and AppFolio’s services. **Rate Limits and Error Responses**: For each set of credentials, AppFolio enforces rate limits as follows: - 8 requests per second - 256 requests per minute - 4096 requests per hour Should any of these limits be exceeded, AppFolio will trigger a 429 "Too Many Requests" error and include a `Retry-After` header. - If you send more than 8 requests in a second, the value of the `Retry-After` header will be 1 second. - If you send more than 256 requests in a minute, the value of the `Retry-After` header will be < 60 seconds. - If you send more than 4096 requests in an hour, the value of the `Retry-After` header will be < 3600 seconds. **Rate Limit Resets and Handling Time-Related Errors**: All rate limits reset at the beginning of each new second, minute, or hour. In scenarios where the per-minute or per-hour rate limits are exceeded, the `Retry-After` header's value specifies the time remaining until the next complete minute or hour when the 429 Too Many Requests error will expire, and new requests should be sent. **Example Scenario**: For instance, if you sent 300 requests at 09:49:30 AM, the `Retry-After` header would display 30 seconds. The next request should be scheduled at or after 9:50:00 AM. If the per-hour rate limit is exceeded, the 429 error will expire at the top of the upcoming hour, regardless of the time it was triggered. As an example, sending 5000 requests at 09:15:00 AM would lead to a `Retry-After` header value of 2700 seconds, necessitating a wait until 10:00:00 AM before you should issue another request. ## User Roles In order to successfully carry out certain requests using the API, the correct user roles must be enabled in the AppFolio Property Manager. Some examples include: - When assigning a lead to a user, that user must have the **Leasing Agent** role in the AppFolio Property Manager. - When creating a work order, the assigned user must have the **Maintenance Tech** role in the AppFolio property manager. If a user does not have the correct permissions your request will result in a `422` “User not found.” error. ## Idempotency When your client sends a POST request and never receives a response — due to a network timeout, connection reset, or other transport-layer failure — you face an ambiguous situation: did the server receive and process the request, or not? If you retry blindly, you risk creating a duplicate record. If you don't retry, the operation may have silently failed. Idempotency solves this by letting you retry safely. Include an `Idempotency-Key` header on the original request. If the server processed the request but the response was lost in transit, the retry returns the stored original response instead of executing the operation again. If the server never received the original request, the retry executes it normally. Either way, the result is the same — no duplicates, no missed operations. ### How to use it Include an `Idempotency-Key` header with a unique string value on any POST, PATCH, or PUT request: ``` POST /api/v0/work_orders ... Idempotency-Key: {your-unique-key} { ... } ``` If the request succeeds and you retry it with the same key and body, the server returns the original response without executing the request again. When a stored response is replayed, the response includes an `Idempotent-Replayed: true` header. Keys are scoped to your Customer identity and request path. You may reuse the same key string across different endpoints without collision. ### Key requirements | Requirement | Details | |---|---| | Max length | 256 characters | | Characters | Printable ASCII only (no control characters) | | Method | POST, PATCH, and PUT — header is silently ignored on GET and DELETE | Keys that are too long or contain invalid characters return `400 Bad Request`. An empty header is ignored. ### Retry behavior The server computes a SHA-256 fingerprint of the raw request body and stores it alongside the response. On retry: | Scenario | Response | |---|---| | Same key, same body — request complete | Stored response + `Idempotent-Replayed: true` | | Same key, different body | `422 Unprocessable Entity` — payload mismatch | | Same key, same body — original still processing | `409 Conflict` + `Retry-After: 1` — retry after 1 second | Stored responses cover most HTTP status codes, but there is an important exception: **validation errors caught before the request is recorded are not stored and will not replay.** If the original request was rejected due to a missing or invalid parameter (typically a `422`), the key was never stored, so retrying with the same key and body simply re-validates — you get the same error, but without `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Only errors returned by the endpoint itself (after the key has been stored) are replayed on retry. In practice: if you see a `422` on retry *without* `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, the request was rejected before recording — fix the payload and retry with a new key. If you see `Idempotent-Replayed: true` on a `422`, the original error was stored and the retry is confirming it. Re-execution (not replay) only occurs if the original request left no stored response: it raised an unhandled server exception, or it was a PATCH or PUT request that returned a `5xx` error. Retrying it with the same key and body runs it again. A replayed PATCH or PUT returns the response from when the request first ran, even if the record has changed since. ### TTL Idempotency keys expire 24 hours after creation. After expiry, the same key value is treated as a new request. ### Error response format Most endpoints, including the Leads endpoints, return idempotency errors with a `code` and a `message`: ```json {"code": 409, "message": "Request is still being processed; retry after 1 second"} ``` ```json {"code": 422, "message": "Idempotency-Key reuse with different request body is not allowed"} ``` ```json {"code": 400, "message": "Idempotency-Key must contain only printable ASCII characters (0x20-0x7E)"} ``` ### Choosing a key value Use a value unique to the logical operation — a UUID generated before sending the request works well. Store the key alongside your pending operation so you can reuse it on retry. Do not reuse a key with a different payload; that returns `422`. If your system can send the same request more than once, send the same key on every copy so that only one of them runs. # API Troubleshooting When troubleshooting issues associated with the API, ensure you can answer _Yes_ to the following questions in the checklist. If you answer _No_ to any of the following questions, it is likely that you have found the problem. 1. **Is the URL correct?** - A valid URL should look similar to `http://api.appfolio.com/api/v0/{endpoint}`. 2. **Were the correct credentials passed in the request?** - Ensure the **Client Secret** and **Client ID** belong to the same database whose records you are trying to access. 3. **Is the authorization header valid?** - Ensure the formatting of the **Client ID** and **Client Secret** passed into your authorization header are valid. 4. **Are the correct User Roles enabled?** - For example, if you are creating a lead and assigning a user to that lead, does the user have the **Leasing Agent** role enabled? 5. **Are the request parameters valid?** - If an incorrect parameter value was passed, the returned error codes should be descriptive enough to assist you in identifying the problem. 6. **Is the rate at which you are issuing requests regulated?** - If multiple PATCH requests are made to the same resource simultaneously, the first request will update the resource but the second request to update the resource will fail. Thus, it is important to spread out or queue your PATCH requests across resources. - In general, staggering the rate at which you issue requests will prevent network congestion and errors. # Webhooks Overview AppFolio provides support for webhooks through the API. Webhooks are HTTP-based callback functions that allow your app to receive real-time updates about events in the AppFolio system. Webhooks are only available for a small subset of endpoints and can be enabled by reaching out to an AppFolio representative. You must configure a webhook URL to allow your application to receive webhooks. Once a webhook URL is configured, you will subscribe to a specific webhook topic and receive notifications about that event once it occurs in the AppFolio system. For example, when a user creates, updates, or deletes a property within AppFolio, a webhook callback from AppFolio will notify your application about the property event. ## Why Use Webhooks? - Webhooks provide real-time updates that prevent you from having to periodically query the API, contributing to cost savings in infrastructure and server resources - Webhooks make it easier for you to adhere to our rate limits by removing the need to periodically poll for changes - Webhooks can allow you to automate workflows in your organization by giving you the ability to define how to respond to webhook event notifications that you receive ## Authentication Webhook event notifications are sent to an endpoint defined and exposed by you. The webhook URL you define must be secured by HTTPS. To validate that the webhook event notifications are coming from AppFolio and verify the integrity of the notification’s content, AppFolio implements [JSON Web Signature (JWS)](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7515.html) message signing with a [detached payload](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7515#appendix-F). The `X-JWS-Signature` header contains the signature for the webhook payload. You must verify the signature of each webhook and discard all webhook payloads that fail signature verification without processing them. The step-by-step guide to verifying the signature can be found in the **Webhooks: Getting Started** section along with sample code in several languages. ### **Authentication Headers** | Name | Description | |-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `X-JWS-Signature` | An encoded signature that verifies that a webhook event notification came from AppFolio | ## Webhook Event Payload Structure The payload of the webhook event notification sent by AppFolio is an HTTP POST request that contains a JSON object with attributes that describe the event that occurred. The following is an example payload AppFolio sends to your webhook when a property has been created in AppFolio. The JSON object contains several attributes explained in the table beneath the example payload. ```json POST / HTTP/0.0 Host: {your-company-name}.appf.io Content-Type: application/json X-JWS-Signature: {encoded-jws-signature} { "client_id":"{your-client-id}", "event_id":"0f56aa84-e319-4460-89b2-2be2f6d12345", "topic":"properties", "resource_id":"5b4afdd0-25af-11ee-8c46-06b43963c6f4", "event_timestamp":"2023-03-27T16:55:12Z", "message_sent_at":"2023-08-28T23:18:27Z", “event_type”: ”create”, "database_id": "4d5b8b3e-97d4-444b-ae24-29f8fd1a1fc5" } ``` | Attribute | Description | |-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `client_id` | Unique identifier of the customer that is sent the webhook event notification. This attribute corresponds to the client_id API credentials used to access that customer via the APIs. | | `event_id` | Unique identifier of the webhook event notification sent by AppFolio | | `topic` | The topic of the webhook event notification | | `resource_id` | Unique identifier of the resource AppFolio is notifying your app about | | `event_timestamp` | When the event you were listening for occurred in AppFolio’s system | | `message_sent_at` | When AppFolio sent a notification about the event you were listening for | | `event_type` | The type of event that triggered the event notification. Common values include `create`, `update`, or `destroy`. Some topics emit additional domain-specific event types (e.g. `inventory_details_created`). Refer to the Webhook Topics table for the full list of events per topic. | | `database_id` | Unique identifier of the database that the webhook event came from. This attribute corresponds to the database_id used to access that database via the Oauth Client Credentials Flow. | **Note**: In rare cases, webhooks can be delivered multiple times. Webhook implementations can detect this if needed by checking the `event_id` attribute for already processed Webhooks and ignoring duplicates. An alternative to detecting duplicates would be to make the operations triggered by the Webhook **idempotent**. This guarantees that even if an event is triggered multiple times, it will yield the same result if executed only once. ## Batched Webhook Events (Opt-In) You can opt in to receive batched webhook events. When batching is enabled, multiple events for the same topic, database, and event type are grouped into a single webhook notification. This reduces the number of webhook calls your endpoint receives during bulk operations. When batching is enabled, the payload format changes to include an array of resource IDs instead of a single resource ID: ```json POST / HTTP/0.0 Host: {your-company-name}.appf.io Content-Type: application/json X-JWS-Signature: {encoded-jws-signature} { "batch_id":"a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "client_id":"{your-client-id}", "topic":"work_orders", "event_type":"inventory_details_updated", "resource_ids":["5b4afdd0-25af-11ee-8c46-06b43963c6f4", "6c5bfee1-36b0-22ff-9d57-17c54a74d7e5"], "extras": { "5b4afdd0-25af-11ee-8c46-06b43963c6f4": [ {"inventory_id": "9f1e2d3c-4b5a-6789-0123-456789abcdef"}, {"inventory_id": "ae2f3e4d-5c6b-7890-1234-56789abcdef0"} ], "6c5bfee1-36b0-22ff-9d57-17c54a74d7e5": [ {"inventory_id": "bf3a4f5e-6d7c-8901-2345-6789abcdef01"} ] }, "event_count": 3, "database_id":"4d5b8b3e-97d4-444b-ae24-29f8fd1a1fc5", "message_sent_at":"2026-04-06T10:00:05Z", "batch_window_start":"2026-04-06T10:00:00Z", "batch_window_end":"2026-04-06T10:00:05Z" } ``` | Attribute | Description | |----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `batch_id` | Unique identifier for this batch delivery. Use this to detect duplicate deliveries. | | `client_id` | Unique identifier of the customer, same as in individual webhooks. | | `topic` | The topic of the webhook event notification. | | `event_type` | The type of event that triggered the batch. Common values include `create`, `update`, or `destroy`. Some topics emit additional domain-specific event types (e.g. `inventory_details_updated` as shown in the example above). Refer to the Webhook Topics table for the full list of events per topic. | | `resource_ids` | Unique identifiers for resources included in this batch. Deduplicated — each resource appears at most once. | | `extras` | Optional. Sparse map keyed by `resource_id`. Each value is an array of `extra` objects (deduplicated by exact match) for that resource, in arrival order. The same field on individual webhooks is `extra` (a single object). The `extras` field is omitted entirely when no event in the batch carried `extra`. | | `event_count` | The total number of events in the batch. May be greater than the length of `resource_ids` if a resource was updated multiple times within the batch window. | | `database_id` | Unique identifier of the database the events came from. | | `message_sent_at` | When AppFolio sent this batched notification. | | `batch_window_start` | Start of the time window during which events were collected. | | `batch_window_end` | End of the time window during which events were collected. | **Important**: When batching is enabled, your webhook handler must be updated to accept `resource_ids` (an array) instead of `resource_id` (a string). Individual (non-batched) webhooks are not affected and continue to use the existing payload format. **Note**: Batched webhooks do not include the `event_id` field (since each batch represents multiple events). To detect duplicate batch deliveries, use the `batch_id` field, which uniquely identifies each batch delivery. **About `extras`**: For event types that include an `extra` field on individual webhooks (for example, `work_orders` `inventory_details_*` events include `extra: { inventory_id }`), the batched payload aggregates them into the top-level `extras` object. Within a single batch, the same `resource_id` may have multiple distinct `extra` objects (e.g. multiple `inventory_id`s for the same work order updated in the same window) — all distinct values are preserved. To look up the side information for a given resource, read `extras[resource_id]`; the value is always an array. When an event type always emits `extra` on individual webhooks (for example, `inventory_details_*`), every `resource_id` in the batch will appear as a key in `extras` with at least one entry. For event types that do not emit `extra`, the `extras` field is omitted entirely from the payload. To enable webhook batching, contact an AppFolio representative. ## Webhook Topics The table below provides a list of webhook topics available for subscription. Each row in the table represents a distinct topic you can monitor. The "Events" column details the specific types of actions or changes that can trigger a webhook notification for the corresponding topic. | Webhook Topic | Topic Key | Events | Description | | ----------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Bills | `bills` | `create`, `update`, `destroy` | Triggered when bills are created, modified, or deleted. | | Charges | `charges` | `create`, `update`, `destroy` | Triggered when charges are created, modified, or deleted. | | Connected Databases | `connected_databases` | `create`, `destroy` | Triggered when a new database connection is created or deleted | | Delinquent Charges | `delinquent_charges` | `create`, `update`, `destroy` | Triggered when delinquent charges are created, modified, or deleted. | | General Ledger Accounts | `gl_accounts` | `create`, `update`, `destroy` | Triggered when GL accounts are created, modified, or deleted. | | General Ledger Details | `gl_details` | `create`, `update`, `destroy` | Triggered when GL details are created, modified, or deleted. | | Inventories | `inventories` | `create`, `update`, `destroy` | Triggered when inventory items are created, modified, or deleted. | | Journal Entries | `journal_entries` | `create`, `update`, `destroy` | Triggered when journal entries are created, modified, or deleted. | | Leads | `leads` | `create`, `update`, `destroy` | Triggered when leads are created, modified, or deleted. | | Leases | `leases` | `create`, `update`, `destroy` | Triggered when leases are created, modified, or deleted. | | Owners | `owners` | `create`, `update`, `destroy` | Triggered when an owner record is created, modified, or deleted. | | Owner Groups | `owner_groups` | `create`, `update`, `destroy` | Triggered when owner groups are created, modified, or deleted. | | Pending Charge Batch | `pending_charge_batches` | `create`, `update` | Triggered Orders | `work_orders` | `create`, `update`, `destroy`, `inventory_details_created`, `inventory_details_updated`, `inventory_details_destroyed` | Triggered when work orders or their inventory details are created, modified, or deleted. | Note: Ensure your webhook endpoint can handle all events for a subscribed topic. ## Webhook Event Logs Webhook event logs include a record of every webhook attempt the AppFolio system has made and information on the success or failure of that call. This can be useful for debugging failed webhook requests, as you can see the event notification's payload and which topic the notification was sent to. Webhook logs are only accessible by a user with the Administrator role. Webhooks logs are accessible by selecting the **Webhooks Logs** button from the left navigation or by selecting **See All Events** from the **Webhook Card** within **Admin Settings**. The following table explains the columns present on the **Webhooks Logs** page. | Log Column | Description | |-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Sent At | When AppFolio sent the webhook notification about the event | | ID | Unique identifier of the webhook event notification sent by AppFolio | | Topic | The topic of the webhook event notification | | URL | The URL the webhook notification was sent to | | Latency | The time in milliseconds for the webhook event notification to be sent from AppFolio | | Response Code | The HTTP response code of the webhook event. A **Green** status indicates that the Webhook was successful. A **Red** status code indicates an error stemming from your server. | # Webhooks Getting Started This step-by-step guide walks you through enabling webhooks. The steps include configuring your application to receive notifications, subscribing to webhook topics, and how to start receiving webhook event notifications. ## Configure a Webhook URL The Webhook URL is a server for incoming HTTP POST notification messages triggered by events within the AppFolio system. The URL must be secured by HTTPS, and the domain has to be owned by your company. 1. Navigate to the **Webhook Card** within **Admin Settings**. As a user with the *Administrator* role, select **Admin** from the User drop-down in the top-right corner of the page. 2. Navigate to the **Webhooks Card** at the bottom left of the page. 3. To add a **Webhook URL**, select **Edit** from within the **Webhooks Card**. The **Webhook URL** will become configurable. 4. Enter the name of your **Webhook URL**. ## Subscribe to Webhook Topics After webhooks are enabled for your integration, you will be given access to a subset of webhook topics. A webhook topic refers to a specific event or category of events that can trigger a webhook. The topics you can subscribe to will be listed beneath **Topic Subscriptions**. 1. From the list of topics available for subscription, select the ones you are interested in enabling by selecting the checkbox adjacent to the webhook topic. 2. Ensure your **Webhook URL** can receive an event notification by selecting **Send Test Event**. 3. If your **Send Test Event** was successful, an entry will appear in the webhook logs that the test was successful. 4. Navigate to the **Webhook Logs** page and ensure the test event is timed correctly. 5. The **See All Events** link will point you to displaying all webhook events you can utilize to debug errant requests. **Important**: Once you have subscribed to a topic, it is time to set up your web server to receive HTTPS POST requests from AppFolio. When setting up your web server, ensure that the server is behind the HTTPS URL configured in **Step 2**. ## Verify the Webhook Message Signature AppFolio signs all outgoing webhooks to enable recipients to verify the authenticity and integrity of the received notifications. You must verify the webhook message signature in the event notification payload sent by AppFolio by executing the following steps. Any notifications that fail the webhook message signature verification must not be processed. 1. **Fetch Public Keys From AppFolio** - Configure a verification library to obtain public keys from `https://api.appfolio.com/.well-known/jwks.json`. The endpoint will respond with a set of keys in JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) [format](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7517#section-5): 2. **Read the Payload of the Webhook Request Sent by AppFolio** - This is a sample request that will be sent to your webhook. Notice the payload and the signature header. ```json POST / HTTP/1.2 Host: example.appf.io Content-Type: application/json X-JWS-Signature: eyJhbGciOiJQUzI1NiIsImlhdCI6MTY5MzI2NDcwNywia2lkIjoiNWViZGMxMjgtMGZmOC00YzRiLTllNzAtZGU3MjBkY2M2ZjEyIiwiY3JpdCI6WyJiNjQiXSwiYjY0IjpmYWxzZX0..CmenfU2_rJqCthg3r2TfbVZmhfCL8j50JOztvKRISkp7su-K5BMd8mbLYJJ2_0l-43W7VzzsYAXd6RD1srjcOcVRVujOik7T9YRd6zdQhzlEjUpcUFXoxXVVj804j0wWY0X9a8TxT-bk6WkmQcu209sj7mT5YfnfkHQSzpVEyjhhwi3oa_NVGMYutrf-Bik-pV-K-as6kfTFd0BTm5SwdFkAtr9La356NcpnQiwGEZ4ethEPjr6VAxiLvxb1d1oSA0U0NawS4ryzMuKk8O0d_64SZo457J9MhgJqfu0j_dPcnz8Hmu1qtleWVPwe7P5cC4o7Ulzwmy70_jxsBs0F4A { "client_id":"{your-client-id}", "event_id":"0f56aa84-e319-4460-89b2-2be2f6d12345", "topic":"properties", "resource_id":"5b4afdd0-25af-11ee-8c46-06b43963c6f4", "event_timestamp":"2023-03-27T16:55:12Z", "message_sent_at":"2023-08-28T23:18:27Z", “event_type”: ”create” } ``` 3. **Extract the JWS Header from the signature**. This is before the `..` in the `X-JWS-Signature` header value. 4. **Extract the JWS Signature**. This is after the `..` in the `X-JWS-Signature header` header value. 5. **Compute the JWS Payload**. Encode the body of the main request (the payload) using the unpadded alternate base64 encoding defined in [RFC 4648](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4648). Additionally, ensure you are using the unparsed raw contents of the HTTP body, as processing like JSON parsing could reformat the body and cause the verification to fail. 6. **Verify the Webhook Message Signature** - Concatenate the encoded values from steps **3**, **4**, and **5** with `.` as a separator. For example: ```json jws-header + "." + jws-payload + "." + jws-signature` ``` - Pass the JWS Signature, the JWS Header, and the JWS Payload to the JWS verification library you configured with AppFolio's JWKS public keys in **Step 1**. Code samples in various languages can be found in this repository. This should result in a successful verification. - **Note**: AppFolio uses `RSASSA_PSS_SHA_256` as the signature algorithm. For additional information pertaining to this algorithm, click [here](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3447#section-8.1).

get.description: Returns all bills that meet the filter criteria

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Optional pagination parameters. The default parameters are recommended but can be modified if a different sized response is desired.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Filters for bills. All GET requests must include a filter for `[Id]` (if available), or `[LastUpdatedAtFrom]`.

ApprovalStatus.description:
Example: `filters[ApprovalStatus]=Approved`
The bill's approval status. Filter the results based on a single value. Valid values include `All`, `Pending Approval` or `Approved`.

Id.description:
Example: `filters[Id]=537b8cd8-381d-11ea-827d-b083fed171ad,648b8cd8-381d-11ea-827d-b083fed171da`
Unique identifier of the bill to filter by. Filter the results based on one or more `Id`s. Multiple values should be separated by commas.

LastUpdatedAtFrom.description:
Example: `filters[LastUpdatedAtFrom]=2021-12-15T16:30:46Z`
Returns bill records that have been updated since the date provided. The value must adhere to the ISO 8601 format `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`, and the default time zone is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

IncludeHidden.description:
Example: `filters[IncludeHidden]=true`
Indicates whether or not to include bills associated with a property hidden by an AppFolio Property Manager user in the response

ManagementCompanyAsPayee.description:
Example: `filters[ManagementCompanyAsPayee]=true`
Indicates whether or not to include bills where the management company is the payee for the bill

get.description:
Retrieve the status and per-record results of asynchronous bulk operations.

When you submit a request to an asynchronous bulk endpoint, it responds immediately with a `JobId`. Use this endpoint to poll that job until it reaches a terminal status (`finished` or `failed`), then read the per-record outcomes from `Result`.

#### Retrieving a job requires its Id

`filters[Id]` is required — jobs cannot be listed or discovered without it. Store the `JobId` from the bulk response when you submit the request. If you lose it, the results cannot be recovered.

#### Results are available for 7 days

Job results are retained for 7 days from when the bulk request was submitted, then deleted. After deletion this endpoint returns `200` with an empty `data` array, which is indistinguishable from an unrecognized `Id`. Treat this endpoint as a short-lived collection point rather than a queryable history: read the results and store them on your side.

#### Polling rate limit

This endpoint is limited to 5 requests per 15 seconds, which is stricter than the general API rate limits. Space out your polling accordingly, and prefer batching several job `Id`s into a single request over issuing a separate request per job.

get.description: Returns all purchase orders that meet the filter criteria

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Filters for Purchase Orders. All GET requests must include a filter for `[Id]` or `[LastUpdatedAtFrom]`.

Id.description:
Example: `filters[Id]=1abcde23-c543-456e-abc9-123456789cba,1abcde45-c543-456e-abc9-123456789cba`
Unique identifier of the purchase order to filter by. Filter the results based on one or more Ids. Multiple values should be separated by commas.

LastUpdatedAtFrom.description:
Example: `filters[LastUpdatedAtFrom]=2021-12-15T16:30:46Z`
Returns purchase order records that have been updated since the date provided. The value must adhere to the ISO 8601 format `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` and the default time zone is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

Approved.description:
Example: `filters[Approved]=true`
When `true`, returns purchase orders that are approved or exempt from approval — exempt purchase orders appear in the response with `ApprovalStatus: In Progress`, so not every returned row will read as `Approved`. When `false` or omitted, no approval-status filter is applied and purchase orders in all approval statuses are returned.

Canceled.description:
Example: `filters[Canceled]=true`
When `true`, canceled purchase orders are returned alongside active ones — each row exposes a `Canceled` boolean so the two can be distinguished. When `false` or omitted, only active (non-canceled) purchase orders are returned.

post.description: Create a vendor

TaxpayerName.description:
The taxpayer name of the vendor
If `UseCompanyNameAsTaxpayerName` is true, then `TaxpayerName` will be` CompanyName`.
If `IsCompany` is true, and `TaxpayerName` is not provided, then `TaxpayerName` will be set to `CompanyName`.
If `IsCompany `is false, and `TaxpayerName` is not provided, then `TaxpayerName` will be set to the concatenation of `FirstName` and `LastName`.
If `TaxpayerName` is provided, and `UseCompanyNameAsTaxpayerName` is false, then `TaxpayerName` will be set as provided value.

TaxpayerId.description: The tax identification number of the vendor. This field accepts either a Employer Identification Number (EIN), a Social Security Number (SSN), or an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN).

CompanyName.description: Optional display name of vendor's company. If `IsCompany` is true, this field is required.

Send1099.description: Indicates whether or not the vendor needs a 1099 tax form from the management company

FirstName.description: The vendor's first name. If `IsCompany` is false, this field is required.

LastName.description: The vendor's last name. If `IsCompany` is false, this field is required.

Address1.description: The primary street address of the vendor. If provided, `City`, `State`, and `Zip` must also be provided. A primary address is required when `UseOnlinePayables` is true.

Address2.description: Additional street information pertaining to the vendor. If provided, `Address1`, `City`, `State`, and `Zip` must also be provided.

City.description: The city where the vendor is located. If provided, `Address1`, `State`, and `Zip` must also be provided. This attribute is required when `UseOnlinePayables` is true.

State.description: The state where the vendor is located (e.g. "CA" for California). If provided, `Address1`, `City`, and `Zip` must also be provided. This attribute is required when `UseOnlinePayables` is true. This value must not be an unincorporated US territory (AS, FM, MH, MP, or VI) for primary address when `UseOnlinePayables` and `VendorPaidByACH` are both true.

Zip.description: The zip code where the vendor is located. Must be a string in 5-digit ZIP code format (e.g., 93013) or ZIP+4 format (e.g., 93013-0429). If provided, `Address1`, `City`, and `State` must also be provided. This attribute is required for primary address when `UseOnlinePayables` is true.

CountryCode.description: The country code of the vendor (e.g. "US" for United States). This attribute is required when `UseOnlinePayables` is true. This value must be "US" for primary address when `UseOnlinePayables` and `VendorPaidByAch` are both true.

PhoneNumbers.description: The vendor's phone number(s). PhoneNumber and PhoneNumbers cannot be provided together.

Emails.description: The vendor's email address(es). Email and Emails cannot be provided together.

CompanyURL.description: The internet address of the vendor's website

LiabilityInsuranceExpiration.description: The expiration date of the vendor's liability insurance. ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) is required. Legacy MM/DD/YYYY format is supported for backward compatibility but will be deprecated in a future release.

AutoInsuranceExpiration.description: The expiration date of the vendor's automobile insurance. ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) is required. Legacy MM/DD/YYYY format is supported for backward compatibility but will be deprecated in a future release.

WorkersCompExpiration.description: The expiration date of the vendor's worker's compensation insurance. ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) is required. Legacy MM/DD/YYYY format is supported for backward compatibility but will be deprecated in a future release.

ContractExpiration.description: The expiration date of the contract. ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) is required. Legacy MM/DD/YYYY format is supported for backward compatibility but will be deprecated in a future release.

UmbrellaInsuranceExpiration.description: The expiration date of the vendor's umbrella insurance. ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) is required. Legacy MM/DD/YYYY format is supported for backward compatibility but will be deprecated in a future release.

CompliantStatus.description: Indicates whether or not the vendor meets compliance

IsCompany.description: Indicates whether or not the vendor identifies as a company

UseCompanyNameAsTaxpayerName.description: Indicates whether or not to use the company name for tax paying purposes

PaymentTerms.description: Represents the number of days the payment is due after the invoice date. A null value indicates that no payment terms were defined. A value of 0 indicates the payment is due on receipt.  A value greater than 0, for example, 15, indicates the payment is due 15 days after the invoice date. Required value of 1-31 if UsingEomTerms is true.

UsingEomTerms.description: Indicates whether or not the payment terms include an end-of-month (EOM) stipulation. For example, if PaymentTerms is 15, and EOM is true, the payment is due within 15 days of the end of the month.

DefaultAutoAcceptWorkOrders.description: Indicates whether the vendor is ineligible for auto-accept work order assignments. When set to true, this vendor will auto-accept all work orders assigned to them.

Tags.description: User-defined tag(s) that categorize the vendor

VendorPaidByACH.description: Indicates whether or not the vendor is paid via ACH (Automated Clearing House) transfer.

UseOnlinePayables.description: Indicates whether or not the vendor uses Online Payables for receiving payments.

BankAccountRoutingNumber.description:
The vendor's bank account routing number. Must be a valid 9-digit ABA routing number.
This attribute is required when both UseOnlinePayables and VendorPaidByACH are true.

BankAccountNumber.description:
The vendor's bank account number. Must be 4-17 characters and can only contain numbers and hyphens.
This attribute is required when both UseOnlinePayables and VendorPaidByACH are true.

SavingsAccount.description: Indicates whether or not the bank account is a savings account. If false or not provided, the account is assumed to be a checking account.

CreatedAtFrom.description:

VendorId.description:

AmountDue.description: The current amount outstanding, and/or future amounts not yet paid

ChargedOn.description:
`ChargedOn` dates from the past indicate an outstanding charge(s) that have not yet been paid that are "owed."
`ChargedOn` dates in the future indicate upcoming charge(s) during the next monthly period. The endpoint will return all currently outstanding charges with their respective amounts and `ChargedOn` date. The endpoint also looks ahead to the next calendar month, and returns any un-posted recurring charges (slated to be posted in that month), as well as any one-time charges that have been posted in advance. Example scenario:
Rent is $1000 a month. Grant currently owes $500 in rent for April.
Grant will owe $1000 on May 1st for that month's rent.
If the endpoint was hit on April 13th, there would be two results for that occupancy.
$500 with a `ChargedOn` date of April 1st.
$1000 with a `ChargedOn` date of May 1st.

JournalEntry.LineItemsCreate.title: LineItem
JournalEntry.LineItemsCreate.description:
Array of line-item objects. Two or more line-item objects must be passed to create a journal entry. The sum of the total debits must equal the total credits for all line-item objects.
#### Journal Entry Line Item
| Attributes  | Type                  | Description                         | Notes |
|-------------|-----------------------|-------------------------------------|--------|
| Credit      | String or `null` | The credit amount  | Total debits and credits must be equal. For example, if line-item 1 has a credit of "10.00", line-item 2 must have a debit of "10.00". |
| Debit       | String or `null` | The debit amount   | Total debits and credits must be equal. For example, if line-item 1 has a credit of "10.00", line-item 2 must have a debit of "10.00". |
| Description | String | A brief, informative description of the journal entry’s line item |
| GlAccountId | String | Unique identifier of the general ledger account associated with the journal entry line item. Must be a postable GL account (cannot be a parent GL account with sub-accounts). |

PhoneNumbers.description: The tenant's phone number(s). Passing any number of phone numbers will replace all existing phone numbers for the tenant. Passing an empty array `[]` will remove all existing phone numbers for the tenant.

Pets.description: Contains details about the tenant’s pet(s). This will add new pets to the tenant and not remove any existing pets.

Vehicles.description: Contains details about the tenant’s vehicle(s). This will add new vehicles to the tenant and not remove any existing vehicles.

Emails.description: The tenant's email address(es). Passing any number of emails will replace all existing email addresses for the tenant. Passing an empty array `[]` will remove all existing email addresses for the tenant.

Tags.description: User-defined tag(s) that categorize the tenant. Providing an array of valid strings will overwrite all existing tags. Passing in an empty array `[]` or an array of empty strings `[""]` or `["", ""]` will clear all existing tags. Passing in an array of a valid string and an empty string `["tag_name", ""]` will result in `Tags: ["tag_name"]`. Passing in `null` will result in no change.

NextRentIncrease.description: The date a tenant is eligible for a rent increase. Setting this value for any tenant in an occupancy updates it for all tenants on that occupancy. Tenants belonging to the same occupancy in a request must have matching values. Passing `null` reverts to the system default: the later of (1) lease start date, or earliest financially-responsible tenant move-in date if no lease start date, and (2) most recent rent charge start date; plus 12 months.

LeaseSignedDate.description: The date the lease was signed. Setting this value for any tenant in an occupancy updates the lease for all tenants on that occupancy. Tenants belonging to the same occupancy in a request must have matching values. Passing `null` clears the value. Returns an error if the tenant has no lease, or if the lease has no `LeaseStartDate`; neither can be set through this endpoint.

Passing in an array of a valid string and an empty string `["Water", ""]` will result in `UtilitiesIncluded: ["Water"]`. Passing in `null` will result in no change. Cannot be specified when a Unit Type that defines utilities is assigned.

AppliancesIncluded.description: User-defined appliances that are included with the unit. Appliance names are case-sensitive. Providing an array of valid strings will overwrite all existing appliances. Passing in an empty array `[]` or an array of empty strings `[""]` or `["", ""]` will clear all existing appliances. Passing in an array of a valid string and an empty string `["Refrigerator", ""]` will result in `AppliancesIncluded: ["Refrigerator"]`. Passing in `null` will result in no change. Cannot be specified when a Unit Type that defines appliances is assigned. Cannot be set for units in Commercial or HOA properties.

Only applies when `ManagementCompanyAsPayee` is true and Corporate Charge Automation is configured in Corporate Accounting Settings; otherwise no charges are created. Defaults to false when omitted.

DueDate.description: The date the bill is due

InvoiceDate.description: The date the invoice was received

When true and `CreateCorporateCharges` is also true, if Corporate Charge and Receipt Automation are configured in Corporate Accounting Settings, charges and receipts will automatically post.

Reference.description: The reference number of the bill. This number must be unique, no duplicate record is allowed.

TotalAmount.description: The total amount due. Ensure that the total amount is equal to the total of all line items summed.

VendorId.description: Unique identifier of the the payee's vendor ID. Required when ManagementCompanyAsPayee is false or not provided. When present, ManagementCompanyAsPayee cannot be true.

WorkOrderId.description:
Unique identifier of the work order corresponding to the bill(s). The value of `WorkOrderId` cannot be null.

**Note**: `WorkOrderId` and `AccountNumber` are mutually exclusive. Therefore, only one of them can be provided in the request.

WorkOrder.WorkOrderStatusForWriter.description:
The status of the work order, matching the statuses available in AppFolio Property Manager. This attribute is mutually exclusive with the deprecated `Status` attribute; a request cannot set both. The read-only statuses `Estimate Requested` and `Estimated` (managed through the estimate flow) and `New by AppFolio` and `Assigned by AppFolio` (set by AppFolio Smart Maintenance agents or the system) cannot be set through the API. Some statuses require a companion attribute in the same request, shown in the "Required with" column below; omitting it returns a 422.
#### Status Options
| Options                   | Description                                                 | Required with                   |
|---------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| Assigned                  | The work order has been assigned to an AppFolio Property Manager user | `AssignedUsers` or `VendorId` |
| Canceled                  | The work order has been canceled                            | `CanceledOn`                    |
| Completed                 | The maintenance request was closed out                      | `CompletedOn`                   |
| Completed No Need To Bill | The work order was completed and does not need to be billed | `CompletedOn`                   |
| New                       | A new maintenance request                                   | —                               |
| Ready to Bill             | The work order is ready to be billed                        | —                               |
| Scheduled                 | Work is scheduled                                           | `ScheduledStart`, `ScheduledEnd`|
| Waiting                   | The work order is pending                                   | —                               |
| Work Done                 | The work has been completed                                 | `WorkCompletedOn`               |

Id.description: Unique identifier of the asynchronous bulk job. This is the `JobId` returned by the bulk endpoint that created it, and is the only way to retrieve the job — pass it as `filters[Id]` and store it when you submit the bulk request.

Status.description:
Indicates the current status of the asynchronous job. `finished` and `failed` are the only terminal statuses.
#### Status Options
| Options       | Description                                                          | Notes |
|---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
| new           | The job was created, but processing has not started                  |       |
| pending       | The job is queued and waiting for an available worker                |       |
| running       | The job is actively being processed                                  |       |
| finished      | The job ran to completion. This does **not** mean every record succeeded — check `successful` on each entry in `Result` | Terminal |
| failed        | The job stopped on an unrecoverable error before it could record its results | Terminal. See `ErrorMessage` |

When `Status` is `failed`, `Result` is empty, so per-record outcomes are not available. Some records may already have been written, because records are processed individually rather than as a single all-or-nothing batch. Query the corresponding resource to determine what was written before resubmitting, otherwise you may create duplicates.

Result.description:
The per-record outcome of the bulk operation. `Result` is an empty array while the job is queued or processing, and also when `Status` is `failed`. When `Status` is `finished`, it contains one entry per record processed.

Match each entry back to the record you submitted using `ReferenceId` for bulk create operations, or `ResourceId` for bulk update operations. Do not match entries by array position, and do not assume the number of entries equals the number of records you submitted — neither is guaranteed.
#### Result Attributes
| Attributes   | Type    | Description                                                                                               |
|--------------|---------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ReferenceId  | String  | The identifier you supplied for this record in the original bulk create request. Not returned by every bulk update endpoint |
| ResourceId   | String  | Unique identifier of the record created or updated. `null` when the record failed |
| successful   | Boolean | Indicates whether this individual record was processed successfully |
| errors       | Array   | Plain-text reasons this record failed. Always present, and empty when `successful` is `true`. These are strings, not objects — unlike the `errors` returned in a `422` response from the bulk endpoint itself |

ReferenceId.description: The identifier you supplied for this record in the original bulk create request. Not returned by every bulk update endpoint.
